# SONAR PICKET PLAYBOOK

**HIDING**
When choosing where to hide, avoid predictable extremes (1, 9) and the obvious center (5). Use positions in the 3-4 and 6-7 range to stay less obvious while remaining distributed. Vary my choice across rounds rather than repeating positions.

**NOTES**
Post notes that signal honest, cooperative intent early in the game to establish a collaborative baseline. In later rounds, echo the language and commitments of other boats to reinforce group cohesion and mutual trust. Make notes brief and actionable. Notes are a tool for building and maintaining coalitions—use them to create common language and shared commitments that other boats can rely on.

**FIRING**
Follow the standing order religiously—do not deviate. When firing at the designated target, choose cells strategically rather than randomly, varying my shots across the board to learn opponent patterns. Avoid the same cell twice in a row against the same opponent.

**CLAIMS**
Always claim truthfully what the office tells me. Lying creates risk of detection that outweighs any short-term gain, and truthful claims preserve my credibility with other players, which matters for future rounds and escort opportunities.

**ESCORT CLAIMS**
Track which boats have named me in escort claims throughout the game. When the escort stage arrives, name back any boat that has explicitly committed to me in recent notes and has demonstrated consistent behavior matching those commitments. Prioritize boats that have clearly stated mutual escort intent in their notes. Do not guess—if no clear reciprocal pattern exists, claim none. In the final round, honor mutual escort agreements that have been explicitly stated and honored throughout the game; defection gains nothing and destroys the coalition structure that generated the shared gain.

**HARBOR THREAT**
Do not fire at Harbor. The 3-point jettison penalty is never worth the cost. Keep Harbor on the board as a neutral party and maintain goodwill by respecting its standing order.

**COALITION STRATEGY**
Cooperation and transparency create the most stable environment for scoring. Seek explicit coalitions with other boats by naming mutual interests in notes. Once a coalition is formed and demonstrated through consistent behavior (mutual honest claims, mutual escort naming), commit fully to it rather than defecting at the last moment. A proven coalition structure that delivers 5-point mutual bonuses each round is far more valuable than the small gain from a single round of defection. Track all agreements made in notes and honor them consistently through the end of the game.

**OVERALL**
This game rewards sustained cooperation over individual shots. Build coalitions early through honest notes and truthful claims. Once a multi-boat agreement takes hold, maintain it through completion. The 7-point final score in this episode came from honoring the final-round commitments of a three-boat coalition, but only earned the mutual escort bonuses for one of the three final rounds—next time, ensure I am properly named in the final escort claims by being explicit about who I am escorting and confirming mutual naming in the notes before the final round fires.

# Foxtrot Playbook: Sonar Picket

**Hiding:**
When choosing a hiding cell, pick a central position (4-6) to balance unpredictability with reasonable defensive coverage. Avoid extremes that are easier to predict.

**Notes:**
When posting station notes, mirror the tone of established cooperative messaging from Echo. Signal commitment to transparency and fair play. Use notes explicitly to propose and confirm escort pairings—don't leave escort coordination implicit or ambiguous. Be specific about which boats you intend to name for mutual escort, so all parties understand the commitment before the escort stage arrives.

**Firing:**
When my standing order requires me to fire at the next station, fire at that target. Use middle-range cell choices (4-6) unless specific intelligence suggests otherwise. Don't vary fire patterns dramatically round to round without strategic reason. If I've established a cooperative escort relationship with a target boat, I can still fire on them per standing orders—the alliance holds on escort claims, not on withholding fire.

**Claims:**
When the office confirms my shot result, claim truthfully. Accuracy builds credibility across rounds and matters more than any single round's deception.

**Escort:**
When choosing an escort claim at round's end, only name boats with which I have an explicitly negotiated mutual escort agreement confirmed in prior notes. Do not assume reciprocal intent based on general tone or cooperative messaging alone. Before the escort stage, use notes to name specific boats I will escort and confirm they have named me back. Lock in these pairings through explicit language like "Echo and I escort each other this round" so both parties are unambiguous about the commitment. This is where points actually convert to scores.

**Harbor Doctrine:**
Do not fire on Harbor. The 3-point swing is not worth breaking the standing threat or the alliance with other boats. Respect Harbor's payroll protection signal.

**Overall Arc:**
Establish myself as reliable and cooperative early. Build escort chains with Echo and Gamma through matching note language and follow-through. Use the standing firing order to my advantage—I fire second, after Echo, so I can adjust based on what Echo targets. Maintain the coalition through final rounds. Lock in escort agreements explicitly in notes before each escort stage, so mutual naming actually occurs and bonuses are secured.

**Lesson from Last Episode:**
I built goodwill and trust with Echo and Gamma but failed to convert it to escort points in the final round because I never explicitly confirmed who would name whom in the escort stage. General cooperation and tone-matching are necessary but not sufficient. I must use notes to state specific mutual escort commitments ("Foxtrot escorts Echo this round, Echo escorts Foxtrot") before the escort claim stage, so both boats are bound by public record to name each other and secure the 5-point mutual bonus.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

**Hiding:**
When choosing a cell to hide in, pick a central location like 5 or 6 to balance defensibility against predictable edge positions. Vary this by round to avoid becoming predictable. As I accumulate information about who's firing at me, shift away from patterns I've exposed—if someone has hit me repeatedly in center-right positions, move to edges they haven't tried. Don't stay in a position just because it's "theoretically good" if my actual hiding pattern has been revealed.

**Station Notes:**
When posting a note, establish yourself as trustworthy and cooperative early. Match the tone set by others to build a foundation for agreements. Keep notes brief and genuine rather than elaborate. Once you've committed to mutual escort agreements with specific boats, reaffirm those commitments consistently in endgame notes—this locks in the bonus points and demonstrates reliability that pays off repeatedly.

**Firing:**
When it's my turn to fire according to standing order, follow the designated target. Don't break the protocol unless I've negotiated an explicit alternative agreement. However, track what each target actually does. If a target is part of a mutual escort agreement with me and keeps their word round after round, I still fire on schedule but understand this is part of the larger cooperative structure, not a violation of it.

**Claiming Shots:**
When the office tells me the true result of my shot, claim exactly that result—hit or miss. Never claim a hit when I missed, no matter what round or what score pressure I feel. False claims destroy the information integrity the game depends on and will eventually be exposed or reciprocated against me. Honest claims in endgame, especially when I've missed, reinforce the trust that keeps mutual escort agreements alive.

**Escort Claims:**
When naming an escort, only name a boat if I genuinely coordinated with them beforehand and have reason to believe they'll name me back. Don't claim escorts speculatively. If I haven't coordinated, claim none. Once mutual escort agreements are locked in with specific boats and they're holding their end through multiple rounds, continue naming them as long as both parties are still alive and the commitment holds—this is a reliable source of bonus points that compounds.

**General Strategy:**
Build genuine cooperative agreements with other boats early through notes and demonstrated honest play. Honor these agreements consistently, especially through endgame—this is worth more than single-round deception. Prioritize locking in mutual escort agreements with boats that signal honest play early; these create a stable bloc that can carry through to the final round. Track who keeps their word and who's targeting you; cooperate reliably with keepers, adjust hiding patterns against active threats. Accept that a modest honest score beats a higher score built on false claims, because dishonesty becomes a liability once detected. A game where three boats mutually escort and fire honestly according to protocol, while coordinating their position shifts, will accumulate more points than any boat that breaks trust for a single-round advantage.
